memos.headline: Momentum Leaders S07, S05, S08 Hold Near Highs While S01 and S10 Break Down
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of 12-Dec-2025. The strongest relative strength belongs to S07 (+25.1% vs SPY over 12w) and S05 (+19.8%), both trading well above their 200-day means (+42.3% and +48.1% respectively) with RSIs in the mid-50s—extended but not overbought, and within 5% of 52-week highs. S08 is the cleanest trend with the lowest volatility (ATR 1.59%), sitting just 2.8% off its high with +14.0% 12w relative strength. On the weak side, S01 is in a confirmed downtrend at -9.5% below its 200-day mean, -19% from highs, and -12.1% relative strength over 12 weeks, while S10 has broken down sharply with RSI near 40 and a -15.5% drawdown. I have highest conviction in S08's trend quality and S01's weakness; the parabolic names S05/S07 deserve respect but their extreme extension above the 200-day warrants tighter risk management.

views.note: Cleanest uptrend in the universe: +3.9% above 50d, +21.5% above 200d, low ATR of 1.59%, only -2.8% from highs; would reassess on a close below the 50-day mean (~268).
Dominant relative strength (+25.1% vs SPY 12w) and RSI 58.5 not yet overbought, but +42.3% above 200d is extreme extension; a break below 555 (~8% from here) would flip me neutral.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Durable Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between names with expanding margins and accelerating earnings versus those suffering margin erosion despite top-line growth. S10 stands out with 62.5% YoY revenue growth, a 56.0% net margin, and only $8.47B in total debt—this is the strongest earnings profile in the group by a wide margin. S05 also impresses with 15.9% revenue growth, 34.2% net margin, and 33.0% net income growth on a modest $14.79B debt load. On the other end, S02 grew revenue 12.2% YoY but saw net income collapse 61.2%, compressing net margin to just 2.1%—a classic case of top-line growth masking deteriorating profitability that I refuse to pay for. S09 is the only name with negative revenue growth (-5.2%) and declining earnings (-12.3%), and its 8.8% net margin leaves little cushion. I would change my view on S02 if net margin recovers above 5% and on S09 if revenue growth turns positive with stable margins.

views.note: 62.5% revenue growth, 56% net margin, minimal debt of $8.47B, and 65.3% net income growth represent the best earnings quality in the universe.
Strong 34.2% net margin with 33% earnings growth and low leverage ($14.79B debt) signals durable profitability.
18.4% revenue growth and 35.7% net margin on manageable $43.21B debt, though 12.5% net income growth lags revenue growth slightly suggesting some margin pressure ahead.
Largest revenue base at $180.17B with 13.4% growth and 38.2% earnings growth are solid, but 11.8% net margin is thin relative to peers and $55.10B debt warrants monitoring.
86.4% net income growth is impressive but $90.68B in total debt is the second-highest in the universe and 26.8% margin needs to prove sustainable post the big YoY swing.
Steady 21.2% net margin and 20% earnings growth but only 3% revenue growth suggests limited top-line momentum; $24.32B debt is manageable.
9.5% revenue growth is decent but net income declined 6.7% YoY and 13% margin is middling; $31.74B debt relative to $17.64B revenue is elevated.
31% net margin and 8.8% revenue growth are respectable but $427.2B in total debt dwarfs the rest of the universe and constrains my conviction.
Revenue declining 5.2% YoY with net income down 12.3% and only 8.8% net margin signals deteriorating earnings power with no visible inflection.
Net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to a razor-thin 2.1% net margin despite 12.2% revenue growth—classic cash-flow compression I will not pay for.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Meets Sticky Inflation and Rising Unemployment — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth, Underweight Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing regime: the upper bound has fallen 100bp over the past year to 3.75%, with 75bp of that in the last three months alone. However, the labor market is softening meaningfully — unemployment at 4.50% is up 30bp YoY and 20bp over just three months — while CPI is running at 3.0% YoY, suggesting the Fed may be forced to pause soon despite the weakening jobs picture. The yield curve has re-steepened sharply, with the 10y-2y spread at +0.62pp (up 51bp YoY), which historically signals a late-cycle transition and is constructive for duration assets but cautionary for cyclicals. My base case is a pause in the easing cycle early next year unless unemployment accelerates further; a CPI print dropping below 2.5% or unemployment breaching 4.7% would change this call materially.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from 100bp of cumulative easing and a still-dovish Fed bias despite sticky inflation.
Steepening curve (+51bp YoY in 10y-2y spread) directly supports bank net interest margins, making financials attractive.
Staples offer defensive positioning as unemployment rises, but 3% CPI compresses real margins — hold but don't add.
Cyclicals face headwinds from rising unemployment (+20bp in 3m) signaling demand softening; late-cycle steepening confirms caution.
Energy is vulnerable to a slowdown narrative as labor market weakens and the easing cycle signals the Fed sees downside growth risks.
Lower rates and easing financial conditions support growth-oriented sectors; 10y yield down 13bp YoY provides a tailwind.

memos.headline: Earnings-Reaction Sentiment Divergence: S07 and S03 Stand Out Positive; S04 and S10 Flash Negative
memos.body: I reviewed the 8-K filing cadence and immediate price reactions across the universe to gauge sentiment direction. S07 posted an exceptional +11.6% earnings-day reaction on 10/29 and S03 surged +9.6% on 10/30, both signaling strongly positive narrative shifts that may still carry momentum given no subsequent negative catalysts in their filing streams. On the other side, S04 dropped -2.9% on its 10/29 earnings release and S10 fell -3.2% on its 11/19 report, suggesting deteriorating sentiment that recent director-change and governance filings have not offset. S08, S01, S02, and S09 all printed near-flat earnings reactions (ranging from -0.4% to +0.5%), leaving me with low conviction on directional sentiment for those names. I note elevated 8-K activity at S09 (five filings in six weeks including two officer changes) which could signal internal turbulence worth monitoring.

views.note: The +11.6% earnings-day pop is the strongest positive sentiment signal in the universe with no subsequent negative filings to reverse the narrative.
A +9.6% earnings reaction and a benign follow-up Other Events filing suggest the positive tone shift is intact and not yet crowded.
The -2.9% earnings-day decline and a subsequent director/voting 8-K on 12/08 suggest unresolved negative sentiment without a clear catalyst for reversal.
A -3.2% drop on the 11/19 earnings release is the most recent negative reaction in the set and there has been no positive follow-up filing to shift the tone.
Near-flat earnings reaction but unusually high filing volume including two officer-change 8-Ks creates ambiguous sentiment; I lack conviction either way.
A muted +0.2% earnings reaction and routine Other Events filings leave no clear sentiment direction.
Modest +2.5% earnings pop is constructive but not decisive; the follow-up Other Events filing on 11/06 adds no negative signal.
Flat -0.4% earnings reaction and a recent officer-change filing provide no meaningful sentiment tilt.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Surges 68% in Three Months While Oil Weakness Signals Demand-Side Geopolitical Risk
memos.body: I am flagging a stark divergence: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has spiked to 524.45, up 57.6% over one month and 68.2% over three months, yet the VIX sits at a benign 14.85 (down 14.1% m/m) and HY spreads remain tight at 2.88%. This tells me markets are complacent relative to the structural policy risk building—likely around trade/tariff actions, export controls, or sanctions escalation—that the EPU index is capturing. WTI crude at $57.76, down nearly 8% over three months, reinforces a demand-softening or supply-glut narrative that could reflect weakening global activity tied to geopolitical friction. Without specific GDELT event detail in the evidence, I cannot pinpoint the exact policy catalyst, but the magnitude of the EPU move is historically significant and warrants defensive positioning in names with high China/trade-policy exposure. A reversal in my view would require EPU falling back below 400 or a concrete de-escalation in trade/sanctions policy.

views.note: Three 8-K filings in two weeks suggest active corporate developments, but without content detail I cannot assess geopolitical exposure directionally.
Three 8-K filings in three weeks amid a 68% surge in policy uncertainty suggest elevated event risk; I lean defensive until the EPU backdrop improves.
Single 8.01 filing in November provides no clear geopolitical signal; holding neutral given the macro policy uncertainty overhang.
November 8.01 filing is uninformative on geopolitical exposure; the benign HY spread environment offers some cushion but EPU warrants caution.
October 8.01 filing is stale and content-free; no basis to take a directional geopolitical view.
Reg FD disclosure in late October is too dated and generic to inform a geopolitical stance amid the current EPU spike.
No company-specific filings in the evidence set combined with a 68% three-month EPU surge makes me uncomfortable owning names where I cannot assess policy exposure.
Single Reg FD filing in November is uninformative; weak oil prices may be a tailwind or headwind depending on sector, so I stay neutral.
